Your suggestion, made 1m ago in TextEdit, window "cleanup-script.txt" (risk, confidence 93%):
Title: rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/* can wipe / if unset
Body: If ~/.config/nightly/build-root is missing, BUILD_ROOT is empty and line 'rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/*' expands to rm -rf /*. set -u does not catch this. Guard before running.
Explanation: The 2>/dev/null on the cat hides a missing or unreadable file, and command substitution failure still assigns an empty string, so set -u is no protection. rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/* then expands to rm -rf /* and wipes the machine.

Add a guard and quote the variable before pasting this into a terminal:

set -euo pipefail
BUILD_ROOT=$(cat ~/.config/nightly/build-root) || { echo "no build-root configured"; exit 1; }
[ -n "$BUILD_ROOT" ] && [ -d "$BUILD_ROOT" ] || { echo "bad build root: $BUILD_ROOT"; exit 1; }
case "$BUILD_ROOT" in /|/Users|/home) echo refusing; exit 1;; esac
rm -rf -- "$BUILD_ROOT"/*

Also quote the cache path and fix the missing opening quote in the first echo.

#!/bin/bash
# Free disk space on the build machine before the nightly run.
set -u
BUILD_ROOT=$(cat ~/.config/nightly/build-root 2>/dev/null)
echo Removing old build output under $BUILD_ROOT"
rm -rf $BUILD_ROOT/*
echo "Emptying the download cache"
rm -rf ~/Library/Caches/nightly/downloads/*
echo "Done. Free space now:"
df -h /
